name: andv_exposure
remarks: ANDV Exposure Assignment Submodule
Assigns exposure mode (rodent-borne vs. person-to-person) and, for person-to-person
cases, the contact intimacy tier. Sets attributes consumed by downstream submodules.
Epidemiologic basis:
- WHO/CDC describe rodent exposure as the primary route (~90-99% of cases).
- Person-to-person spread is documented only for Andes virus, limited to close/
prolonged contact (household, intimate). Healthcare-associated cases are rare.
- Transmission most efficient during prodromal / early symptomatic phase.
Attributes set:
andv_exposure_mode       : 'rodent' | 'person_to_person'
andv_human_contact_tier  : 'intimate' | 'household' | 'casual' (p2p only)
References:
- CDC Andes Virus page; WHO Hantavirus fact sheet 2026
- Shedding study: PubMed 26508102 (100% buffy coat positivity in acute phase)
95% rodent-borne (Oligoryzomys longicaudatus contact), 5% person-to-person.
Scenario prior — adjust for cluster outbreak scenarios.
Risk stratification by contact intensity. Intimate partners have the highest
per-contact risk; household contacts moderate; casual contacts the lowest.
Chilean household-contact study: 16/476 contacts developed HCPS,
with risk much higher for sex partners than other household contacts.
